tcgshop.fact.1: Every great collection starts like the Pokédex: with number 001, Bulbasaur.
tcgshop.fact.4: Number 004 matches Charmander. May your collection burn bright!
tcgshop.fact.7: Number 007 matches Squirtle. Your collection is starting to make waves.
tcgshop.fact.10: Number 010 matches Caterpie, the first Pokémon Ash caught in the anime.
tcgshop.fact.25: Number 025 matches Pikachu, the most famous Pokémon in the world!
tcgshop.fact.39: Number 039 matches Jigglypuff. It would sing with joy... even if everyone fell asleep.
tcgshop.fact.52: Number 052 matches Meowth. With this many cards, that's quite a Pay Day!
tcgshop.fact.60: 60 cards is exactly the size of a standard Pokémon TCG deck.
tcgshop.fact.94: Number 094 matches Gengar, who is surely peeking at your collection from your shadow.
tcgshop.fact.100: Number 100 matches Voltorb. Careful, don't explode with excitement.
tcgshop.fact.102: 102 cards: the same number as the original 1999 Base Set.
tcgshop.fact.108: Number 108 matches Lickitung... and Spiritomb is made of 108 spirits.
tcgshop.fact.129: Number 129 matches Magikarp. Everyone underestimates it until it evolves. Like your collection.
tcgshop.fact.133: Number 133 matches Eevee: as many evolutions as ways to sort a binder.
tcgshop.fact.143: Number 143 matches Snorlax, blocking the road... to your next pack.
tcgshop.fact.150: Number 150 matches Mewtwo, the Pokémon created by science.
tcgshop.fact.151: 151! The same as the original Kanto Pokédex, which ends with Mew.
tcgshop.fact.197: Number 197 matches Umbreon, star of some of the most expensive modern cards.
tcgshop.fact.249: Number 249 matches Lugia, guardian of the seas.
tcgshop.fact.250: Number 250 matches Ho-Oh: they say whoever sees it finds eternal happiness.
tcgshop.fact.251: Number 251 matches Celebi, who closes the Johto Pokédex. Your collection travels through time.
tcgshop.fact.282: Number 282 matches Gardevoir, willing to protect its trainer with its life.
tcgshop.fact.384: Number 384 matches Rayquaza, lord of the skies.
tcgshop.fact.386: Number 386 matches Deoxys, who closes the Hoenn Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.448: Number 448 matches Lucario, who can sense the aura... of rare cards.
tcgshop.fact.493: Number 493 matches Arceus, who according to myth created the universe.
tcgshop.fact.500: Half a thousand different cards! Emboar, number 500, celebrates big.
tcgshop.fact.570: Number 570 matches Zorua, who could pass for any of your cards.
tcgshop.fact.649: Number 649 matches Genesect, who closes the Unova Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.658: Number 658 matches Greninja, the ninja master of Kalos.
tcgshop.fact.700: Number 700 matches Sylveon, the Fairy-type Eeveelution.
tcgshop.fact.721: Number 721 matches Volcanion, who closes the Kalos Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.778: Number 778 matches Mimikyu, who just wants to be loved... like your common cards.
tcgshop.fact.809: Number 809 matches Melmetal, who closes the Alola Pokédex (and came from Pokémon GO).
tcgshop.fact.888: Number 888 matches Zacian. Triple eight, a lucky number!
tcgshop.fact.898: Number 898 matches Calyrex, who closes the Galar Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.905: Number 905 matches Enamorus, the last Pokémon discovered in Hisui.
tcgshop.fact.999: Number 999 matches Gimmighoul. You'd need 999 of its coins to evolve it.
tcgshop.fact.1000: 1,000 different cards! Gholdengo, number 1000, is made of 1,000 coins. You, of 1,000 cards.
tcgshop.fact.1025: Number 1025 matches Pecharunt, the last Pokémon in the National Pokédex.
tcgshop.fact.1500: 1,500 cards. If each were a Gimmighoul coin, you could evolve one and a half.

tcgshop.grade.odds_note: This table is the base spread. Grade 10 depends on each card's age: 0.45·e^(-1.7A) (45% on a new card, 30% at 6 years, 11% at 21 years); other Grades keep the table's proportions. In sets released up to 2017 (old printing: worse centering and edges) 30% of cards land right on the edge: 4.9, 5.0 or 5.1 (10% each). In the other 70% any Grade of 5.0 or higher, Grade 10 included, comes up with only 0.5% of its chance, so going above 5.1 is almost impossible and many land below 5.0 and lose value when graded. On the right, how much of the jump to Grade 10 is reached: ((Grade-1)/9)^3.

tcgshop.league.rules:
COMPETITIVE TCG MODE

• Deck of up to 20 cards from your collection (max 2 copies, at least 6 Pokémon, at most 6 Items). If you don't save one, it's built from your best cards.
• Every Pokémon has HP, a type and two attacks based on its species and rarity. Non-Pokémon cards are Items: Potion, Research, Switch or Extra Energy.
• You start with 5 cards and your strongest Pokémon as Active. Each turn draw 1, bench Pokémon (max 3), use Items, attach 1 energy and retreat by paying its cost.
• Attacking ends your turn. If the attacker's type is super effective against the defender, it deals +20.
• A knockout scores 1 point (2 for ex: Double Rare or higher). First to 3, or leaving the rival without Pokémon, wins.
• League matches between players: win or lose ELO points and climb ranks (Bronze → Master). Against the house: a CobbleDollars prize.

tcgshop.ptcg.rules:
REAL POKÉMON TCG

Matches use the twinleaf.gg engine (open source, MIT licence) with the official rules and each card's real effects: 60-card decks, 6 prizes, evolution, typed Energy, weakness/resistance, special conditions, Supporters, Stadiums and Tools.

• Play: from the phone (TCG League → Play) against the AI on 4 levels, League vs AI (points at stake) or find an online opponent. Challenge another player from the Cobblemon wheel (“TCG challenge”) or with /tcgduel <player>. Also at a Play Table.
• League matches (vs the AI or players) give rank points; losing them costs a little money. The Veteran and Champion AIs play top meta decks.
• Your deck is checked before every match: 60 cards, max 4 per name, 1 ACE SPEC, 1 Radiant, banned combos and that you own the copies.
• At the table: click any card to zoom in with its attacks and abilities (attack, use abilities or retreat from there). Drag cards from your hand onto their glowing target; drag your Active onto the Bench to retreat.
• ? (S key) = AI hint · ☰ (L key) = detailed log and concede · Space = end turn · Tab = look at the board during a choice.

tcgshop.gradeinfo.1: A graded card gets a Grade from 1.0 to 10.0 (decimals like 9.5 or 9.9 too). Its price becomes: ungraded price × Mg. Below Grade 5 it loses value; from Grade 5 it gains depending on the card: no fixed multipliers and no added premiums.
tcgshop.gradeinfo.3: First the card's maximum: M10 = min(100, 1 + 99·Z^4), with Z = 0.45A + 0.55Q. From Grade 5: Mg = 1 + (M10 - 1)·((Grade - 1)/9)^3. At Grade 4.9 or lower the card loses value: Mg = 0.40 + 0.59·((Grade - 1)/3.9)^1.5 (Grade 1 = x0.40, Grade 3 = x0.62, Grade 4.9 = x0.99). From Grade 5 the jump is cubic: Grade 5 reaches only 9% of it, Grade 8 47%, Grade 9 70%, Grade 9.5 84% and Grade 10 100%. No card goes above x100 and almost none get there.
tcgshop.gradeinfo.5: A = years since release / 25, between 0 and 1 (Base Set 1999 → A = 1; a 2024 card → A = 0.08). Age only counts here, not in scarcity. Old cards are worth far more at high Grades, but Grade 10 is also harder: chance = 0.45·e^(-1.7A). And if the set came out in 2017 or earlier, 30% of the time the Grade is 4.9, 5.0 or 5.1; otherwise Grade 5.0 or higher is almost impossible (0.5% of its normal chance).
tcgshop.gradeinfo.7: Q = 0.70·Pfinal + 0.15·S + 0.10·R + 0.05·B. For cards without a Pokémon, Pfinal is replaced by T (weights still add up to 1). R = print rarity (Common 0, Double rare 0.25, Illustration rare 0.50, Ultra rare 0.60, Hyper rare 0.85, Special illustration 1; no rarity 0.10). B = artwork appeal (Special illustration 1, Illustration rare 0.85, Ultra rare 0.75, Hyper rare 0.55, Double rare 0.35, others 0.15).
tcgshop.gradeinfo.9: A ranking of 1,025 Pokémon is used (#1 Charizard). The Pokémon is found inside the card name (with prefixes like Alolan or Radiant and suffixes like ex, V or VMAX). If there are several (Tag Team), the most popular counts. P = ((1025 - rank)/1024)^2. Top 300: Pfinal = 0.65 + 0.35·P (never below 0.65). Others: Pfinal = 0.65·((1025 - rank)/725)^2. The Top 300 gets a clear edge because that is what is collected and graded the most, but differences remain outside it. A Pokémon missing from the ranking gets the neutral value of the median Pokémon (#513).
tcgshop.gradeinfo.11: S = 0.45·R + 0.55·E. E = collection scarcity from the real price of its pack: E = ln(pack price / 4.5) / ln(100), between 0 and 1 ($4.5 pack → 0; $450 or more → 1). No print runs are made up.
tcgshop.gradeinfo.13: T = 0.35·C + 0.30·R + 0.20·S + 0.15·U. C = category importance: Supporter 0.85, Item 0.70, Tool 0.55, Stadium 0.50, Special Energy 0.45, Basic Energy 0.10 (unknown 0.50). U = utility = 0.40·K + 0.30·F + 0.20·V + 0.10·H: K = competitive use (copies in the engine's meta decks; most used = 1); F = effect strength and H = historical relevance = 0.5 (neutral, no reliable data); V = versatility (how often the card was reprinted).
tcgshop.gradeinfo.15: Pokémon: depicts a Pokémon; its demand comes from the ranking. Trainer splits into Supporter (strong support effect, usually one per turn), Item (actions and effects during your turn), Tool (attached to a Pokémon for an extra effect) and Stadium (changes the game conditions and can help or hurt both players). Energy: basic or special, pays for attacks and abilities.
tcgshop.gradeinfo.16: #Why can two cards of the same rarity differ at Grade 10?
tcgshop.gradeinfo.17: Rarity is only 10% of Q (plus its share of S). Popularity (70% of Q) and age (45% of Z) weigh the most. Z is also raised to the fourth power: small differences at the top become big price gaps. A Charizard special illustration can multiply its price several times at Grade 10, while the same rarity of an obscure Pokémon from a recent set barely moves.

tcgshop.league.help.points.p1: Your League rating starts at %s and never drops below %s. It decides your rank and your place on the leaderboard.
tcgshop.league.help.points.p2: Only LEAGUE matches change it: League vs the AI, the player queue and play tables. Friendly AI matches and challenges between friends never give or take points.
tcgshop.league.help.ranks.p1: Your best rating (peak) is kept: rank coins and boards unlock with the best rank you ever reached, even if you drop later.
tcgshop.league.help.ranks.now: Now: %s pts (%s) · peak %s · %s pts to reach %s.
tcgshop.league.help.ranks.now_top: Now: %s pts (%s) · peak %s · you're at the top rank!
tcgshop.league.help.ai.cols: "AI pts" is the opponent's rough strength. Win / Lose: fixed League points per level (not ELO). Prize: what you earn when you win. Fine: what you pay when you lose a League match.
tcgshop.league.help.ai.casual: Friendly: doesn't change your points or W-L, no fine, and if you win you get the level's prize and a win against the house.
tcgshop.league.help.ai.ranked: League vs the AI: you win or lose the points in the table; you also get the prize if you win and pay the fine if you lose (never more than you have).
tcgshop.league.help.ai.blocked: As you rank up, easy levels stop being allowed in League: %s. Friendly matches allow any level.
tcgshop.league.help.ai.meta: The Hard AI plays a top meta deck half of the time, and the Champion always does.
tcgshop.league.help.pvp.p1: Between players ELO is used: the winner gains exactly what the loser drops. Beating someone above you gives a lot; beating someone below you gives little.
tcgshop.league.help.pvp.formula: Formula: %s × (1 − chance to win), with a minimum of %s pts per match. Examples:
tcgshop.league.help.pvp.penalty: Losing a League match against another player costs %s. The winner gets points, not money.
tcgshop.league.help.pvp.modes: League matches: the phone's "Find opponent" queue and play tables (click a table to wait for an opponent).
tcgshop.league.help.pvp.friendly: Challenges (Cobblemon wheel "TCG Challenge" or /tcgduel) are friendly: no points, no fine.
tcgshop.league.help.stats.wl: W · L: wins and losses in League matches (vs players and League vs the AI).
tcgshop.league.help.stats.ai_wins: Wins against the house: all your wins against the AI, friendly ones included.
tcgshop.league.help.stats.played: Matches played: every match you finish, in any mode.
tcgshop.league.help.stats.streak: Streak: League wins in a row. A League loss resets it and friendly matches don't touch it. Your best streak is kept.
tcgshop.league.help.stats.peak: Peak: the highest rating you ever reached.
tcgshop.league.help.stats.top: Leaderboard: the top 10 by points among players who played at least one League match.
tcgshop.league.help.stats.you: You: %s W · %s L (%s%%) · %s vs the house · %s matches · streak %s (best %s) · peak %s pts.
tcgshop.league.help.rewards.p1: The coin is used for each match's coin flip and the board decorates your table. They unlock by themselves when you meet the condition; equip them with a click in the Coins and Boards tabs.
tcgshop.league.help.rewards.rank: Rank rewards use the best rank you ever reached; peak rewards use your best rating.
tcgshop.league.help.rewards.loot: Loot coins: every pack you open has a %s chance (1 in %s) to give you one you don't have yet.
tcgshop.league.help.rewards.money: Money: beating the AI pays its level's prize (see "Vs the AI"); losing in League costs the fine.
tcgshop.league.help.rewards.goals: The Goals tab shows how far you are from each unlock.
tcgshop.league.help.deck.copies: Max 4 copies with the same name (even from different sets). Basic Energy has no limit and is free: you don't need to own it.
tcgshop.league.help.deck.special: Only 1 ACE SPEC card, 1 Radiant Pokémon and 1 Star card; just one copy of each Prism Star card.
tcgshop.league.help.deck.combos: You can't mix Professor Sycamore, Professor Juniper and Professor's Research, or run Lysandre with Boss's Orders.
tcgshop.league.help.deck.format: The engine also checks the format (special cards); press Check to see it before saving.
tcgshop.league.help.deck.owned: You must own the copies in your General Binder or inventory.
tcgshop.league.help.deck.auto: If you haven't saved a deck, an automatic one is built from your cards when you play.
tcgshop.league.help.editor.counter: Top: X/60 counter. Right: Pokémon / Trainer / Energy split and the curve (Basic, Stage 1, Stage 2; Item, Supporter, Stadium, Tool; Energy by type).
tcgshop.league.help.editor.controls: Click a card: add · Shift+click: every copy · right click: remove · Ctrl+Z: undo · Ctrl+F: search.
tcgshop.league.help.editor.autocomplete: Auto-fill: the engine finishes the deck around what you already added. +Energy: fills with basic Energy of your types.
tcgshop.league.help.editor.check: Check: the engine reviews the deck without saving it. Save: only with 60 cards and no errors.
tcgshop.league.help.editor.warnings: ✖ = error (can't play) · ⚠ = advice (e.g. an evolution without its previous stage) · ✔ = all good.
tcgshop.haggle.hint: Wheel or ↑↓: ±1%% · Type digits to set your price · Enter to confirm
tcgshop.haggle.tip.type: Click or type digits to set the price by hand. Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.quick: Sets your offer to that share of the market price.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.accept: Close the deal at the current price. Leaves the NPC happy.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.counter: Propose your price. Every counter costs some of their patience.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.max: Final word: they take your price or leave. No middle ground.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.market: Argue with the market price. Works if your number is reasonable.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.elsewhere: Tell them they won't find better. Newcomers buy it; experts don't.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.broke: Say you can't pay more. Softens newcomers and casual sellers.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.rep: Brag about your shop's fame: the higher your reputation, the more they'll overpay.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.think: Ask for time. Sometimes they improve the offer; push it and they tire.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.no: Decline politely. Usually leaves a neutral review.
tcgshop.haggle.tip.rude: Decline rudely. Most likely a bad review.
tcgshop.haggle.out.bad: %s versus market: could have gone better
tcgshop.haggle.out.sub.4: Serve people who want a deal sooner.

tcgshop.phoneup.call.title: Daily call

tcgshop.event.inspection.name: Surprise inspection
tcgshop.event.inspection.desc: A trade inspector will drop by the shop today. They'll check the smell, the lighting, nearby monsters, the roof and walls, whether the displays are stocked and whether there are other unfixed problems. A good grade boosts reputation for a day; a bad one lowers it for half a day.
tcgshop.event.inspection.start: You've been told an inspector is coming today. You have a little time to get ready.
tcgshop.event.inspection.fix: Get the shop ready before they arrive: no bad smell (spray), good lighting, no monsters nearby, roof and walls, stocked displays and no other unfixed problems.
tcgshop.event.demanding_customer.name: Very demanding customer
tcgshop.event.demanding_customer.desc: A picky, impatient customer is on the way: they only buy below market price and complain about everything.
tcgshop.event.demanding_customer.start: A very demanding customer is heading to your shop.
tcgshop.event.demanding_customer.fix: Serve them well: put something below market price and check them out quickly. If they leave 3 stars or more, it's solved.
tcgshop.event.overprice_rumor.name: Overpricing rumor
tcgshop.event.overprice_rumor.desc: Word around town is that your shop is a rip-off. Customers see prices as higher than they are and your effective reputation drops a bit.
tcgshop.event.overprice_rumor.start: Someone's going around saying your shop is way too expensive.
tcgshop.event.overprice_rumor.fix: Set reasonable prices (the reputation price factor at 0 or above) and keep them for about 3 minutes.
tcgshop.event.impatient_group.name: Impatient group
tcgshop.event.impatient_group.desc: A group of 3-4 very impatient customers arrives all at once.
tcgshop.event.impatient_group.start: A group of customers in a hurry is coming.
tcgshop.event.impatient_group.fix: Check them out fast (cashier or you at the register) and make sure they find something at a good price. If they average 3 stars, it's solved.
tcgshop.event.troublemaker.name: Troublesome customer
tcgshop.event.troublemaker.desc: A rude customer is coming to haggle and cause trouble: while they're around, other customers arrive in a worse mood.
tcgshop.event.troublemaker.start: A customer looking for trouble is heading to your shop.
tcgshop.event.troublemaker.fix: Right-click them to calm them down, or have a guard: they'll calm them once they've been inside a little while.
tcgshop.event.aggressive_competition.des: A rival shop launched deals: fewer people come today and your prices look a bit more expensive.
tcgshop.event.aggressive_competition.sta: A rival shop has started a price war.
tcgshop.event.aggressive_competition.fix: Make 5 sales at market price or below to prove your prices are good.
tcgshop.event.robbery_wave.name: Robbery wave
tcgshop.event.robbery_wave.desc: There's a gang of thieves in the area: for a few hours, many more thieves come to your shop.
tcgshop.event.robbery_wave.start: Watch out! A gang of thieves is roaming the area.
tcgshop.event.robbery_wave.fix: Hire a guard or place at least 2 theft detectors.
tcgshop.event.distracted_employee.name: Distracted employee
tcgshop.event.distracted_employee.desc: Your cashier has their head in the clouds and checks people out much slower. You can hear them humming.
tcgshop.event.distracted_employee.fix: Right-click your cashier to get them focused again.
tcgshop.event.generous_tip.name: Generous tip
tcgshop.event.generous_tip.desc: A customer will leave a tip (10% extra) on today's next sale.
tcgshop.event.generous_tip.start: Someone's in a tipping mood today.
tcgshop.event.family_shoppers.name: Family of shoppers
tcgshop.event.family_shoppers.desc: A family comes shopping: they don't spend much and prefer packs, but they're in a good mood.
tcgshop.event.family_shoppers.start: A family is coming to your shop.
tcgshop.event.tcg_influencer.name: TCG influencer
tcgshop.event.tcg_influencer.desc: A card influencer visits the shop. If they leave delighted (4-5 stars), more people will come tomorrow; if they leave unhappy, your reputation will feel it.
tcgshop.event.tcg_influencer.start: A card influencer stopped by your shop.
tcgshop.event.returning_customer.name: A regular returns
tcgshop.event.returning_customer.desc: One of your regulars comes back in a great mood and ready to buy.
tcgshop.event.nostalgic_collector.name: Nostalgic collector
tcgshop.event.nostalgic_collector.desc: A collector is looking for cards from old sets and pays gladly (up to a bit above market).
tcgshop.event.nostalgic_collector.start: A collector of old cards stopped by.
tcgshop.event.beginners_day.name: Beginners' day
tcgshop.event.beginners_day.desc: Lots of newcomers are getting into cards: more regular customers come and they're keener on packs.
tcgshop.event.beginners_day.start: It's beginners' day! Lots of people want to start a collection.
tcgshop.event.wholesale_buyer.name: Wholesale buyer
tcgshop.event.wholesale_buyer.desc: A buyer wants to take several things at once (up to 3), as long as they're not far above market.
tcgshop.event.wholesale_buyer.start: A wholesale buyer visited your shop.
tcgshop.event.word_of_mouth.name: Word of mouth
tcgshop.event.word_of_mouth.desc: Your good reviews are spreading around town: more people come today.
tcgshop.event.word_of_mouth.start: People are talking about your shop around town.
tcgshop.event.loyalty_bonus.name: Loyalty bonus
tcgshop.event.loyalty_bonus.desc: Your regulars reward you: a little money for each of them (capped) and some snacks.
tcgshop.event.loyalty_bonus.start: Your regulars left you a little something.
tcgshop.event.collectors_day.name: Collectors' day
tcgshop.event.collectors_day.desc: Collectors are out today: more wealthy collectors and more people wanting to trade cards.
tcgshop.event.collectors_day.start: Collectors' day! Lots going on today.
tcgshop.event.good_ambience.name: Great atmosphere
tcgshop.event.good_ambience.desc: People love your shop's decoration: +3 reputation for the day.
tcgshop.event.good_ambience.start: People love the atmosphere in your shop.
tcgshop.event.outstanding_employee.name: Outstanding employee
tcgshop.event.outstanding_employee.desc: Your cashier is on a roll: they check people out much faster today.
tcgshop.event.spotless_shop.name: Spotless shop
tcgshop.event.spotless_shop.desc: No bad smells and no monsters nearby: customers notice and reputation rises +3 for the day.
tcgshop.event.spotless_shop.start: Your shop is spotless and it shows.
tcgshop.event.small_sponsorship.name: Small sponsorship
tcgshop.event.small_sponsorship.desc: A local business sponsors your shop: a bit of money in the register and a good name.
tcgshop.event.small_sponsorship.start: A local business wants to sponsor your shop!
tcgshop.event.set_collector.name: Set collector
tcgshop.event.set_collector.desc: A collector is hunting cards from one particular set (the one you display most) and may take several.
tcgshop.event.set_collector.start: A collector looking for a specific set stopped by.
tcgshop.event.international_collector.de: A collector from abroad wants to complete a set: they take up to 3 cards and pay up to a bit over market.
tcgshop.event.international_collector.st: An international collector visited your shop.
tcgshop.event.lucky_day.name: Lucky day
tcgshop.event.lucky_day.desc: Everything goes right today: more wealthy collectors come and people are keener to buy.
tcgshop.event.lucky_day.start: You have a feeling today is going to be a good day.
tcgshop.event.collection_exhibition.name: Collection exhibition
tcgshop.event.collection_exhibition.desc: Your displays draw attention: extra reputation for the day depending on how many you have.
tcgshop.event.collection_exhibition.star: People come to see your displays like it's a museum.
tcgshop.event.legendary_customer.name: Legendary customer
tcgshop.event.legendary_customer.desc: A legendary collector visits the shop: they buy several things and, if they leave 5 stars, your fame grows.
tcgshop.event.legendary_customer.start: A legendary customer stopped by your shop!
tcgshop.event.expansion_party.name: Expansion celebration
tcgshop.event.expansion_party.desc: The new expansion is out! More people come and the newest set sells more eagerly.
tcgshop.event.expansion_party.start: Today we celebrate the new expansion!
tcgshop.event.limited_offer.name: Limited-time offer
tcgshop.event.limited_offer.desc: For a few hours, anything at market price or below sells much better.
tcgshop.event.limited_offer.start: Limited-time offer! Anything at a good price will fly.
tcgshop.event.supplier_discount.name: Supplier discount
tcgshop.event.supplier_discount.desc: The Wholesaler comes to see you and your next purchase (Wholesaler or phone Market) is 15% cheaper today.
tcgshop.event.supplier_discount.start: The Wholesaler is coming with a discount for you.
tcgshop.event.early_delivery.name: Early delivery
tcgshop.event.early_delivery.desc: One of your CobbleGrade orders will arrive quite a bit earlier.
tcgshop.event.early_delivery.start: CobbleGrade has moved one of your orders forward.
tcgshop.event.expert_visit.name: Expert visit
tcgshop.event.expert_visit.desc: A grading expert stops by and leaves you a 20% discount on your next CobbleGrade submission (today).
tcgshop.event.expert_visit.start: A grading expert is coming to the shop.
tcgshop.event.decoration_contest.name: Decoration contest
tcgshop.event.decoration_contest.desc: The town holds a shop decoration contest: if yours is well decorated, there's a small prize.
tcgshop.event.decoration_contest.start: The shop decoration contest has begun.
tcgshop.event.shop_competition.name: Shop comparison
tcgshop.event.shop_competition.desc: A magazine compares card shops: the best rated one gets a good name and a small prize.
tcgshop.event.shop_competition.start: A magazine is comparing card shops.
tcgshop.event.job_seeker.name: Someone's looking for work
tcgshop.event.job_seeker.desc: Someone's looking for a job and comes to offer themselves: today your next hire costs half.
tcgshop.event.job_seeker.start: Someone's coming to ask if you need staff.
tcgshop.event.indecisive_customer.name: Indecisive customer
tcgshop.event.indecisive_customer.desc: A customer looks at everything twice and can't make up their mind.
tcgshop.event.collectors_argue.name: Collectors arguing
tcgshop.event.collectors_argue.desc: Two collectors argue in your shop about prices and cards.
tcgshop.event.collectors_argue.start: Two collectors started a debate in your shop.
tcgshop.event.trade_fever.name: Trading fever
tcgshop.event.trade_fever.desc: Everyone wants to trade cards today: more collectors come with trade offers.
tcgshop.event.mystery_collector.name: Mysterious collector
tcgshop.event.mystery_collector.desc: A mysterious collector examines everything closely but never buys... Maybe someone will come looking for something.
tcgshop.event.mystery_collector.start: A mysterious collector has been looking at your displays.
tcgshop.event.players_meetup.name: Players' meetup
tcgshop.event.players_meetup.desc: Some players are meeting at your play table: they come to play and draw a few more people.
tcgshop.event.players_meetup.start: Some players are meeting at your shop to play.
tcgshop.event.weather_change.name: Change in the weather
tcgshop.event.weather_change.desc: It's raining: fewer people come, but those who do are more patient. Without a roof or walls they get wet and arrive in a worse mood.
tcgshop.event.weather_change.start: The weather has changed and people notice.
tcgshop.event.expansion_announced.name: Expansion announced
tcgshop.event.expansion_announced.desc: A new card expansion has been announced. A celebration is likely in the coming days.
tcgshop.event.expansion_announced.start: A new expansion has been announced!
tcgshop.event.expansion_announced.chat: Customers can't stop talking about it: they say there'll be a launch party soon.
tcgshop.event.photo_visitor.name: Visitor taking photos
tcgshop.event.photo_visitor.desc: Someone wanders around the shop taking photos of everything. Maybe they'll post them online...
tcgshop.event.photo_visitor.start: Someone has been taking photos of your shop.
tcgshop.event.offcatalog_vendor.name: Off-catalog vendor
tcgshop.event.offcatalog_vendor.desc: The black market dealer shows up near you with a pack that isn't in any catalog (they trade it for a Pokémon).
tcgshop.event.offcatalog_vendor.start: Someone in a hood is beckoning you from a corner...
tcgshop.event.supplier_delay.name: Supplier delay
tcgshop.event.supplier_delay.desc: The supplier is running late: the phone Market is 10% more expensive today.
tcgshop.event.supplier_delay.start: The supplier is running late today.
tcgshop.event.collector_seller.name: Collector selling cards
tcgshop.event.collector_seller.desc: A couple of collectors come to sell you cards from their collection (never below market).
tcgshop.event.collector_seller.start: Some collectors are coming to sell you cards.

item.tcgshop.mop.tip: Cleans puddles, droppings and mess in your shop.
item.tcgshop.repair_kit.tip: Fixes sparks, scorch marks, broken registers and displays.
tcgshop.incident.not_owner: Only the shop owner can deal with this.
tcgshop.incident.package.opened: You open the box: %s items inside.
tcgshop.incident.package.empty: The box was empty... (you've opened plenty this week)
tcgshop.incident.need.puddle: You need a mop to dry the puddle.
tcgshop.incident.need.debris: Clear the debris with an empty hand.
tcgshop.incident.need.dirt: You need a shovel to clear the dirt.
tcgshop.incident.need.droppings: You need a mop to clean this up.
tcgshop.incident.need.sparks: You need a repair kit to fix the fault.
tcgshop.incident.need.mess: Pick it up with an empty hand or a mop.
tcgshop.incident.need.package: Open it with an empty hand.
tcgshop.event.power_failure.name: Power Failure
tcgshop.event.power_failure.desc: Sparks fly from the fuse box: the shop is nearly dark and the register won't work for the cashier.
tcgshop.event.power_failure.start: The power just went out in the shop!
tcgshop.event.power_failure.fix: Use a repair kit on the sparks next to the shop core.
tcgshop.event.water_leak.name: Water Leak
tcgshop.event.water_leak.desc: There are puddles on the floor: customers slip, lose patience and buy less.
tcgshop.event.water_leak.start: There's a leak and the floor is filling with puddles!
tcgshop.event.water_leak.fix: Dry every puddle with a mop.
tcgshop.event.register_broken.name: Broken Register
tcgshop.event.register_broken.desc: The register is sparking: the cashier can't ring up packs or boxes (you still can in person).
tcgshop.event.register_broken.fix: Use a repair kit on the sparks next to the register.
tcgshop.event.ac_broken.name: Broken Air Conditioning
tcgshop.event.ac_broken.desc: It's sweltering inside: customers arrive grumpy and give up sooner.
tcgshop.event.ac_broken.fix: Use a repair kit on the sparking unit.
tcgshop.event.stuck_door.name: Stuck Door
tcgshop.event.stuck_door.desc: Some debris is blocking one of the doors: nobody can come in through it.
tcgshop.event.stuck_door.start: One of the doors got stuck!
tcgshop.event.stuck_door.fix: Clear the debris with an empty hand (a few hits).
tcgshop.event.broken_display.name: Broken Display
tcgshop.event.broken_display.desc: A display broke down and nobody can buy from it. Your products are still inside, safe.
tcgshop.event.broken_display.fix: Use a repair kit on the sparks next to the display.
tcgshop.event.messy_stockroom.name: Messy Stockroom
tcgshop.event.messy_stockroom.desc: Boxes are scattered everywhere and nothing can be found: service is slow.
tcgshop.event.messy_stockroom.fix: Tidy the mess with an empty hand or a mop.
tcgshop.event.clumsy_customer.name: Clumsy Customer
tcgshop.event.clumsy_customer.desc: A clumsy customer knocked products to the floor: those display slots can't sell until you pick them up.
tcgshop.event.clumsy_customer.start: A customer who keeps tripping over things just walked in...
tcgshop.event.clumsy_customer.fix: Pick up what fell with an empty hand or a mop.
tcgshop.event.mystery_package.name: Mystery Box
tcgshop.event.mystery_package.desc: Someone left a box by the door. What could be inside?
tcgshop.event.mystery_package.start: There's a mystery box by the door. Open it with an empty hand.
tcgshop.event.mystery_package.fix: Open it with an empty hand before someone takes it.
tcgshop.event.power_failure.var.pichu: A mischievous Pichu is chewing the cables near the register!
tcgshop.event.water_leak.var.roof: Rainwater is dripping through the roof.
tcgshop.event.water_leak.var.squirtle: A playful Squirtle is soaking everything!
tcgshop.event.messy_stockroom.var.zubat: A Zubat got into the stockroom and knocked everything over.
tcgshop.event.mystery_package.var.no_sen: The box has no sender... just your address.
tcgshop.event.clumsy_customer.dropped: Oops! The clumsy customer knocked products off a display.
tcgshop.evline.inc_power.0: Are you closed? It's pitch dark in here.
tcgshop.evline.inc_power.1: I can barely see the cards in this light.
tcgshop.evline.inc_power.4: Is the whole block out of power?
tcgshop.evline.inc_flood.1: I just soaked my new shoes.
tcgshop.evline.inc_flood.2: Is this a shop or a swimming pool?
tcgshop.evline.inc_flood.3: I hope the water doesn't reach the cards.
tcgshop.evline.inc_register.1: I hope I can pay somehow...
tcgshop.evline.inc_register.2: That register is making a weird noise.
tcgshop.evline.inc_register.3: Can I only pay the owner?
tcgshop.evline.inc_register.4: That's going to make a long line.
tcgshop.evline.inc_hot.3: The sleeves are sticking to my hands.
tcgshop.evline.inc_hot.4: I'll buy quickly and go, I'm suffocating.
tcgshop.evline.inc_door.1: I nearly tripped on the debris.
tcgshop.evline.inc_door.2: I had to walk all the way around.
tcgshop.evline.inc_door.4: That door won't budge at all.
tcgshop.evline.inc_door.5: Good thing there was another entrance.
tcgshop.evline.inc_display.1: I wanted to check that display, but I can't.
tcgshop.evline.inc_display.3: I'd better stay away from those sparks.
tcgshop.evline.inc_display.4: Shame, that's where the good stuff was.
tcgshop.evline.inc_display.5: I'll come back when it's fixed.
tcgshop.evline.inc_mess.1: I almost stepped on a box.
tcgshop.evline.inc_mess.2: Did you just get a delivery?
tcgshop.evline.inc_mess.3: Nobody can find anything like this.
tcgshop.evline.inc_mess.5: Looks like a hurricane came through.
tcgshop.evline.inc_clumsy.3: Relax, I didn't break anything... I think.
tcgshop.evline.inc_clumsy.4: Phew, these shelves are so tight.
tcgshop.event.blocked_entrance.name: A Pokémon blocks the entrance
tcgshop.event.blocked_entrance.desc: A huge Pokémon (a sleepy Snorlax, a stubborn Wobbuffet or the Psyduck family) has settled next to the door. While it stays there, customers won't come in through that door and those waiting get impatient sooner. It never covers the doorway itself: you can get through.
tcgshop.event.blocked_entrance.start: There's a huge Pokémon parked next to the shop door!
tcgshop.event.blocked_entrance.fix: Wake it up and get it to leave: right-click with an empty hand many times, give it a berry or, sneaking + right-click, battle it.
tcgshop.event.charmander_scorch.name: Out-of-control Charmander
tcgshop.event.charmander_scorch.desc: A nervous Charmander slipped into the shop and left scorch marks next to one or two displays. Those displays can't be used until you clean the marks. There's never real fire.
tcgshop.event.charmander_scorch.start: A Charmander got in and scorched the displays!
tcgshop.event.charmander_scorch.fix: Clean the scorch marks (repair kit). You can also get the Charmander out: empty hand, a berry or a battle (sneaking + right-click).
tcgshop.event.geodude_rampage.name: Rowdy Geodude
tcgshop.event.geodude_rampage.desc: A Geodude came rolling down from the mountain and left debris next to the displays. Until you clear it up, the shop's decoration counts for less.
tcgshop.event.geodude_rampage.start: A Geodude came rolling in and covered everything in rocks!
tcgshop.event.geodude_rampage.fix: Clear the debris (empty hand or the kit). The Geodude leaves if you shoo it, give it a berry or beat it in battle.
tcgshop.event.psyduck_confused.name: Confused Psyduck
tcgshop.event.psyduck_confused.desc: A Psyduck with a headache bumped into a display and knocked products over. Those slots can't be bought until you sort it out (your items don't move from their place).
tcgshop.event.psyduck_confused.start: A confused Psyduck crashed into a display!
tcgshop.event.psyduck_confused.fix: Shoo it away with an empty hand (right-click a few times), give it a berry or, sneaking + right-click, battle it.
tcgshop.event.jigglypuff_song.name: Singing Jigglypuff
tcgshop.event.jigglypuff_song.desc: A Jigglypuff has decided to give a concert in your shop. Customers arrive in a worse mood and with less patience, and every so often some of those inside leave (putting back what they were going to buy).
tcgshop.event.jigglypuff_song.start: A Jigglypuff is singing in the shop and customers are falling asleep!
tcgshop.event.jigglypuff_song.fix: Get it to leave: right-click with an empty hand, give it a berry or, sneaking + right-click, battle it.
tcgshop.event.murkrow_thief.name: Thieving Murkrow
tcgshop.event.murkrow_thief.desc: A Murkrow made off with something from a display (the cheapest item). That slot looks empty to customers until you get it back. If the event ends before you do, you lose its value from the register. A guard gets it back on their own.
tcgshop.event.murkrow_thief.start: A Murkrow flew in and is going for your displays!
tcgshop.event.murkrow_thief.fix: Shoo it away with an empty hand (right-click a few times) or, sneaking + right-click, battle it. If you have a guard, they'll handle it.
tcgshop.event.diglett_holes.name: Digging Diglett
tcgshop.event.diglett_holes.desc: A Diglett has dug holes all over the shop and left piles of dirt on the floor.
tcgshop.event.diglett_holes.start: A Diglett is digging up your shop floor!
tcgshop.event.diglett_holes.fix: Clean up the dirt (broom or empty hand). You can get the Diglett out with an empty hand, a berry or a battle (sneaking + right-click).
tcgshop.event.pidgey_invasion.name: Pidgey invasion
tcgshop.event.pidgey_invasion.desc: A flock of Pidgey got in through the door and made a mess of droppings all around the entrance.
tcgshop.event.pidgey_invasion.start: A flock of Pidgey has invaded the shop!
tcgshop.event.pidgey_invasion.fix: Clean up the droppings. Shooing the Pidgey (one empty-hand right-click each) stops them bothering people, but what they left is still there.
tcgshop.event.rotom_register.name: Rotom in the cash register
tcgshop.event.rotom_register.desc: A Rotom got into the cash register. Checkout is hit-and-miss: sometimes it's super fast, sometimes it jams.
tcgshop.event.rotom_register.start: A Rotom got into the cash register!
tcgshop.event.rotom_register.fix: If it bothers you, get it out with an empty hand (right-click a few times).
tcgshop.event.meowth_explorer.name: Explorer Meowth
tcgshop.event.meowth_explorer.desc: A curious Meowth came in to sniff around the displays. It doesn't hurt anyone.
tcgshop.event.meowth_explorer.start: A Meowth came in to look around the shop.
tcgshop.event.vulpix_warmth.name: Vulpix seeks warmth
tcgshop.event.vulpix_warmth.desc: It's cold and a Vulpix has curled up in the brightest corner of the shop.
tcgshop.event.vulpix_warmth.start: A cold Vulpix has taken shelter in your shop.
tcgshop.event.combee_flowers.name: Combee in the flowers
tcgshop.event.combee_flowers.desc: Some Combee are buzzing by the entrance, looking for nectar.
tcgshop.event.combee_flowers.start: Some Combee are fluttering by the shop door.
tcgshop.event.pikachu_visit.name: Pikachu visit
tcgshop.event.pikachu_visit.desc: A wild Pikachu is wandering around the shop. Customers love it: a few more come in, and in a better mood, while it's here.
tcgshop.event.pikachu_visit.start: A wild Pikachu came into the shop!
tcgshop.event.eevee_curious.name: Curious Eevee
tcgshop.event.eevee_curious.desc: An Eevee is poking around the displays. Customers are delighted: a few more come in, in a better mood.
tcgshop.event.eevee_curious.start: A curious Eevee is exploring your shop.
tcgshop.event.chansey_kind.name: Kind Chansey
tcgshop.event.chansey_kind.desc: A kind Chansey walks around the shop calming everyone down: customers are more patient and in a better mood.
tcgshop.event.chansey_kind.start: A kind Chansey has come to help in the shop.
tcgshop.event.butterfree_spring.name: Springtime Butterfree
tcgshop.event.butterfree_spring.desc: A Butterfree is fluttering between the displays. It's so pretty it draws in a few more collectors than usual.
tcgshop.event.butterfree_spring.start: A Butterfree came fluttering into the shop.
tcgshop.event.lucky_meowth.name: Lucky Meowth
tcgshop.event.lucky_meowth.desc: A Meowth with a shiny coin on its forehead is wandering the shop. If you pet it or give it a berry, it sometimes drops a coin (nothing big).
tcgshop.event.lucky_meowth.start: A very fancy Meowth came into the shop. Could it be lucky?
tcgshop.event.togepi_family.name: Adorable Togepi
tcgshop.event.togepi_family.desc: A Togepi wandered into the shop and a family is coming to see it. They spend little and prefer packs, but they have a great time.
tcgshop.event.togepi_family.start: An adorable Togepi is in your shop! A family is coming to see it.
tcgshop.event.bulbasaur_gardener.name: Gardener Bulbasaur
tcgshop.event.bulbasaur_gardener.desc: A Bulbasaur has started tending the plants by the entrance. Today the shop's decoration counts a little more (it doesn't place or remove blocks).
tcgshop.event.bulbasaur_gardener.start: A Bulbasaur is tidying up the plants by the entrance.
tcgshop.event.calm_ambient.name: Calm atmosphere
tcgshop.event.calm_ambient.desc: A calm Pokémon (a Psyduck, a sleeping Abra or a Slowpoke) has settled in the shop and everyone relaxes: more patience and better mood. If you touch the Abra, it teleports away.
tcgshop.event.calm_ambient.start: A very calm Pokémon has settled in the shop.
tcgshop.event.flaaffy_glow.name: Glowing Flaaffy
tcgshop.event.flaaffy_glow.desc: A Flaaffy lights up the shop with its glowing tail. If there was a power failure or a short circuit, it fixes it right away.
tcgshop.event.flaaffy_glow.start: A Flaaffy came in and the shop lit up.
tcgshop.event.tropius_fruit.name: Fruity Tropius
tcgshop.event.tropius_fruit.desc: A Tropius is resting by the entrance. If you pet it, it drops some fruit, and if you give it a berry, a few more berries (once each).
tcgshop.event.tropius_fruit.start: A Tropius has come to rest by your shop!
tcgshop.event.guardian_pokemon.name: Guardian Pokémon
tcgshop.event.guardian_pokemon.desc: A strong Pokémon (a Lucario in mountain or snowy areas, a Growlithe elsewhere) guards the entrance all day. No thief will come near today.
tcgshop.event.guardian_pokemon.start: A guardian Pokémon is keeping watch at your shop door.
tcgshop.actor.only_owner: Only the shop owner can deal with this Pokémon.

tcgshop.actor.teleported: %s woke up startled and teleported away!

tcgshop.actor.battle_lost: %s is still in the shop. You can try again.

tcgshop.actor.slots: %s knocked products over: %s slots can't be bought until you sort it out.
